description.narrative:
The Humanitarian impact of the war on Gaza strip has drastically compounded existing vulnerabilities of the Gazan population, wherehumanitarian needs are primarily driven by the protracted Israeli military occupation, 16-year blockage and recurrent hostilities on the Gaza Strip. Prior to the current escalations, the 2023 oPt Humanitarian Response Plan identified 2.1 million Palestinians, of which 1.3 million in the Gaza Strip, as requiring urgent intersectoral assistance in Food, Shelter, WASH, Protection and Education. The heavy and uninterrupted Israeli bombardments on Gaza, compounded by Israel’s water, electricity and fuel cuts on the Gaza Strip,have led to the complete inoperability of basic household and community WASH infrastructure, spoilage ofmarket food supply, and rapid depletion of essential drinking water and household food reserves across all districts in the Strip thus undermining provision oflife-saving services.
The current vulnerabilities are further exacerbated by the massive homes, market and infrastructure destruction that impact the basic needs of hundreds of thousands who returned back from the south of the strip following the ceasefire agreement back in January. Additionally, the lack of sufficient repairs to water infrastructure, coupled with limited storage capacity, continues to undermine water quality, increasing the risk of contamination and associated public health concern. With a high leakage rate in water distribution networks of over 70 per cent associated with extensive damage during 15 months of escalated hostilities, compared with a 50 per cent loss rate prior to October 2023.
With essential sectors, including health, water, and sanitation, on the brink of collapse for 2.3 million residents of Gaza, Oxfam in partnership with a local partner, Palestinian Environment Friends (PEF) a long-standing partner of Oxfam (Annex I – PEF Capacity Assessment) with presence across Gaza Strip, are proposing a 6 month intervention to provide essential and lifesaving water, sanitation <(>&<)> hygiene services to at least 6,500 individuals returned totheir home of origin in North Gaza and Gaza governorates. The proposed project aligns with WASH cluster standards, SPHERE standards, HRP sectorial objectives as well the Flash Appeal Priority Response.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
